title: Why and so: reasons, results and purposes
goal: Give reasons, say what happened as a result and explain what something is for — with *eftersom, därför att, därför, för att* and *så att*, each in its own word order.
bekal: you can give a reason with *eftersom* or *därför att*, and a result with *därför* + inverted verb
you can say what you do something for: *för att* + base form
you can tell *så att* (so that) from *så* (so, and as a result)

dialogs.title: Dialogue — På kvällskursen
dialogs.intro: Tuesday evening. Dian takes Swedish evening classes twice a week; her teacher is Lena, and tonight Dian is the last one through the door. Her classmate Pablo is from Chile.

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Hej Dian! Du är lite sen ikväll.
lines.id: Hi Dian! You're a bit late tonight.
lines.literal: hi Dian! you are a-little late tonight.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Förlåt. Tunnelbanan stod stilla i tjugo minuter, därför kom jag för sent.
lines.id: Sorry. The subway was stuck for twenty minutes, that's why I was late.
lines.literal: sorry. tunnel-railway-the stood still in twenty minutes, therefore came I too late.

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Ingen fara. Sätt dig, vi pratar just om varför vi lär oss svenska.
lines.id: No problem. Sit down, we're just talking about why we're learning Swedish.
lines.literal: no danger. set yourself, we talk just about why we learn ourselves Swedish.

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Pablo, du först. Varför läser du svenska?
lines.id: Pablo, you first. Why are you studying Swedish?
lines.literal: Pablo, you first. why read you Swedish?

lines.speaker: Pablo:
lines.text: Eftersom min sambo är svensk, vill jag kunna prata med hennes familj.
lines.id: Since my partner is Swedish, I want to be able to talk to her family.
lines.literal: since my live-together is Swedish, want I can talk with her family.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jag läser svenska för att få ett bättre jobb här.
lines.id: I'm studying Swedish to get a better job here.
lines.literal: I read Swedish for to get a better job here.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och jag vill stanna i Sverige efter examen, så jag måste kunna språket.
lines.id: And I want to stay in Sweden after I graduate, so I have to know the language.
lines.literal: and I want stay in Sweden after degree, so I must can language-the.

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Utmärkt. Lägg märke till att ni har använt tre olika ord: eftersom, för att och så.
lines.id: Excellent. Notice that you've used three different words: eftersom, för att and så.
lines.literal: excellent. lay notice to that you have used three different words: since, for to and so.

lines.speaker: Pablo:
lines.text: Men vad är skillnaden mellan eftersom och därför att?
lines.id: But what's the difference between eftersom and därför att?
lines.literal: but what is difference-the between since and therefore that?

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Betydelsen är densamma. Men därför att kommer nästan alltid efter huvudsatsen.
lines.id: The meaning is the same. But därför att almost always comes after the main clause.
lines.literal: meaning-the is the-same. but therefore that comes almost always after main-clause-the.

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Då betyder det ”av den anledningen”, och verbet kommer direkt efter: Därför kom du för sent.
lines.id: Then it means "for that reason", and the verb comes straight after it: That's why you were late.
lines.literal: then means it "of that reason-the", and verb-the comes directly after: therefore came you too late.

lines.speaker: Pablo:
lines.text: Så vi pratar svenska så att Lena blir glad?
lines.id: So we speak Swedish so that Lena will be happy?
lines.literal: so we talk Swedish so that Lena becomes glad?

lines.speaker: Lena:
lines.text: Precis! Och därför får ni ingen läxa ikväll.
lines.id: Exactly! And that's why you're getting no homework tonight.
lines.literal: exactly! and therefore get you no homework tonight.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då var det tur att jag kom, trots allt!
lines.id: Then it was lucky I came after all!
lines.literal: then was it luck that I came, despite all!

notes: **Därför kom jag för sent** — *därför* (**DEHR-för**, "that's why, therefore") is an adverb, not a linking word. When it opens the sentence — or the second half after a comma — it takes the first slot, so the verb must follow at once: *därför **kom jag***, never *därför jag kom*. It is exactly the V2 rule from *Idag går jag*. And **komma för sent** is the everyday way to say "to be late (for something)".

**Eftersom min sambo är svensk, vill jag…** — an *eftersom*-clause may open the sentence. The whole clause then counts as **one** element, so the main verb comes next: *…, **vill jag** kunna prata*. The comma is optional. **En sambo** (**SAHM-boo**, from *sammanboende*, "living together") is a partner you live with without being married — a status so common in Sweden that it has its own law.

**För att få ett bättre jobb** — *för att* + the base form of a verb means "in order to" and answers the question *Varför?* with a **purpose**. English often just says "to": *I'm studying Swedish **to** get a job*. Swedish cannot drop the *för*: *för att få*, not *att få*.

**…så jag måste kunna språket** — *så* (**soh**) as "so, and as a result" joins two main clauses, just like *och* and *men*. Careful speakers and writers keep normal word order after it: *så **jag måste***. You will also hear *så måste jag* in fast speech; start with the first one.

**Därför att** means the same as *eftersom*, but it normally stands **after** the main clause and puts a little more weight on the reason: *Jag kom för sent **därför att** tunnelbanan stod stilla.* Both are subordinating words, so BIFF applies: *därför att den **inte** gick*.

**Ingen fara** ("no problem", literally "no danger") is the friendly reply to *förlåt*. **Lägg märke till** = "notice"; **trots allt** = "after all"; **det var tur att…** = "it was lucky that…". And **en läxa** is homework — at SFI and at school alike.

grammars.title: Four ways to say "because"
body: All four words below give a reason. What separates them is the word order they demand and where in the sentence they may stand.

head: Word
Kind
Can it start the sentence?
Example
rows: **Eftersom** jag var sjuk, stannade jag hemma.
Jag stannade hemma **därför att** jag inte mådde bra.
Jag stannade hemma **för att** jag var sjuk.
Jag stannade hemma, **för** jag var sjuk.

after: Turn any of these round and you get a **result** with *därför*: *Jag var sjuk. **Därför stannade jag** hemma.* The cause comes first, the result second, and the verb jumps right after *därför*.

To answer *Varför?* in conversation, Swedes say **För att…** or simply **För…**: *Varför kom du sent? — För att tunnelbanan stod stilla.* Starting an answer with *Eftersom…* is correct but sounds like a written report.

grammars.title: Purpose and result: för att, så att, så
body: *Why* do you do something (purpose)? And *what happens* because of it (result)? Swedish has a separate tool for each.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: Jag sparar pengar **för att** resa till Indonesien.

after: **För att** is a two-faced word: followed by a **base form** it means "in order to" (*Jag kom **för att hjälpa** dig* — I came to help you); followed by a **subject and a verb** it means "because" (*Jag kom **för att du bad** mig* — I came because you asked me). Look at what comes next and you will always know which one you have.

**Så att** is a subordinating word, so BIFF applies: *Jag skriver upp ordet **så att jag inte glömmer** det.* Plain **så** is not, so after it *inte* stays after the verb: *Det regnade, **så vi gick inte** ut.*

blocks.text: Read each row aloud from left to right, then flip it: turn the left column into a *därför* sentence. *Eftersom jag var trött…* → *Jag var trött. Därför gick jag hem.* Ten minutes here will save you months of hesitation.

head: Cause (eftersom …)
Result (därför …)
rows: därför bor vi i ett kollektiv

blocks.title: Three classic mistakes
items: **Därför without inversion.** Not *Därför jag kom för sent*, but *Därför **kom jag** för sent*. *Därför* fills the first slot, so the verb must follow.
**Inversion after eftersom.** Not *eftersom **är jag** sjuk*, but *eftersom **jag är** sjuk*. After a subordinating word the subject always comes first.
**För at the start of a sentence.** Plain *för* can never open a written sentence. If you want to start with the reason, use *Eftersom…*.

blocks.text: **SFI** — *Svenska för invandrare*, "Swedish for immigrants" — is the free Swedish course offered by every municipality to newly arrived adults. Classes are small and wildly international: in one room you may find an engineer from Iran, a nurse from the Philippines and a pensioner from Germany. Dian's evening class works the same way, and Lena's favorite question is always *Varför?*

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 7

Then add a purpose: *Jag skyndade mig för att hinna med tåget.*
